description: Agaricus campestris, the field or meadow mushroom, is a common edible agaric of grasslands worldwide. Its cap is white, the gills are bright pink when young and mature through red to chocolate-brown, and it produces a dark brown spore print. It is closely related to the cultivated button mushroom (Agaricus bisporus).
edibilityNotes: A choice edible that should always be cooked before eating. The critical danger is misidentifying a young, button-stage destroying angel or death cap (Amanita) as a field mushroom: these are DEADLY due to amatoxins, which cause delayed gastrointestinal symptoms 6-24+ hours after the meal followed by apparent recovery and then fatal liver and kidney failure. Amanita species have WHITE gills that never turn pink or brown, a white spore print, and a membranous cup (volva) at a swollen base often hidden below the soil line. Always dig up the entire base to check for a volva, confirm pink-to-brown gills and a dark brown spore print, and avoid any all-white-gilled specimen. Also distinguish the toxic Agaricus xanthodermus (yellow stainer), which bruises chrome-yellow (most strongly at the stem base when cut) and smells unpleasantly phenolic/of ink or carbolic; A. campestris does not stain strongly yellow and smells pleasantly mushroomy. Note that pink-gilled buttons can resemble young Amanita whose gills have not yet been exposed, so spore print and volva checks are essential.
distribution: Widespread and common across temperate regions worldwide, including Europe, North America, and Asia, with introduced ranges elsewhere.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Destroying angel / death cap (Amanita virosa, A. phalloides and allies)
dangerousLookalikes.note: DEADLY (amatoxins; delayed-onset liver/kidney failure). Distinguished by white gills that never turn pink or brown, a white spore print, and a membranous cup (volva) at a swollen base; young button-stage specimens are the most dangerous because they superficially resemble a field mushroom. Field mushrooms have pink-to-brown gills, a dark brown spore print, and no volva.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Agaricus xanthodermus (yellow stainer)
dangerousLookalikes.note: Toxic, causes gastrointestinal upset in many people. Bruises bright chrome-yellow, especially at the stem base when cut, and smells unpleasantly phenolic/of ink or carbolic; A. campestris does not stain strongly yellow and smells pleasantly mushroomy.
